title: process_dio: newer version with inadmissible candidate still clears parent state
description: File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs Lines 341-354. When a newer version DIO arrives, the code checks if the candidate is admissible BEFORE calling adopt_version(). If inadmissible, it returns Rejected. However, this means a node could receive multiple newer-version DIOs from inadmissible candidates and never adopt the new version. Edge case: All neighbors advertising version N+1 have inadmissible ranks. Node stays on version N indefinitely while network moves forward. Fix: Consider adopting version regardless of individual candidate admissibility, then wait for an admissible candidate at the new version.
close_reason: Fixed in rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs process_dio(). A newer DODAGVersionNumber now supersedes the local one unconditionally (RFC 6550 section 8.2.2.4): candidate_admissible() is evaluated first, adopt_version() runs, and only the individual candidate is rejected when inadmissible. The old gate let a node cling to version N indefinitely when every newer-version advertiser had a temporarily bad rank/link, partitioning it from the migrated network. Security unchanged: an attacker could already force adoption by claiming an admissible rank. The old test invalid_newer_version_dio_preserves_parent_state pinned the defective behavior (kept stale version + parents across a version boundary) and was rewritten as inadmissible_newer_version_still_adopts_and_resets_membership (version advances, membership resets: unjoined/INFINITE/empty). New test admissible_newer_version_dio_restores_connectivity_after_bad_ones covers the partition scenario end-to-end: saturated-cost v1 advertiser adopts v1 then an admissible v1 DIO rejoins at rank 512. Discovered during analysis and filed separately: select_parent admissible() lacks the floor/DAGRank checks of candidate_admissible(). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-rpl --lib 139 passed.
